sections.t: Chequered sengis will grow to be around 25–30 cm (9.8–11.8 in) long, excluding their tail, making them one of the longest sengis. Their average tail length is slightly over 25 centimeters, which is slightly shorter than their body length. They commonly weigh around half a kilogram (1.1 pounds), but will sometimes grow to be about 0.7 kg (1.5 lb). Their coat is usually a light to medium brown, but it can range from beige to dark brown.

Chequered sengis are exclusively diurnal and likely monogamous. Chequered sengis that are in a male-female pair build a nest out of leaf litter but spend much of their time apart. They breed year-round and produce up to three young per litter.
The chequered sengi is primarily an insectivore, eating termites, ants, beetles and centipedes. It also will eat mollusks, eggs and small mammals, amphibians and birds.
